To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the number of circulating regulatory T cells (Treg cells), which are potent immune modulatory cells, is decreased in HIV-infected individuals.
the absolute number of regulatory T cells is reduced in the blood and gut of HIV-infected patients but that these cells retain their suppressive function.
Tregs are present in blood and gut of HIV-infected subjects, and that Tregs from HIV-infected patients retain their suppressive function.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of regulatory T cells (Treg) in HIV infection.
the characterization of the frequency and functional status of Treg in HIV-1 infected individuals.
the function and regulation of regulatory T cells (Treg) during HIV infection.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
Tregs are not functionally defective in HIV-1 infection but are quantitatively diminished in chronic progressive disease.
Tregs are not functionally impaired in HIV-1 infection, but their absolute numbers are reduced, especially in chronic progressors.
the absolute number of Tregs is significantly decreased in chronic progressive HIV- 1 infection but not in elite controllers.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
Tregs remain functional in chronic progressive HIV infection, but the number of Tregs is reduced, particularly in gut-associated lymphoid tissues.
Tregs are not dysfunctional in HIV-1 infection but are quantitatively depleted in the blood and tissue of patients with chronic progressive disease.
Tregs are present at lower frequencies in the blood of patients with chronic progressive disease, but their function remains intact in the face of quantitative changes.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the absolute number of Tregs is significantly reduced in blood and gut of HIV-infected individuals with chronic progressive disease, but the suppressive function of these cells is intact.
Tregs in chronic HIV- 1 infection have a preserved suppressive function in spite of their decreased numbers in the blood and gut-associated tissues.
Treg function in the setting of chronic progressive HIV- 1 infection is preserved, but their numbers are decreased.
